## 2026-11-14: a slot gets the names the machine's /etc/hosts gives a forwarded address

**What was wrong.** A runner with `--slot-forward 127.77.0.1:443` gave each private slot a listener at 127.77.0.1:443 on its own loopback, relayed to the machine's registry proxy, but no name pointed there inside the slot. The guest wrote its own `/etc/hosts` with `localhost` alone, so `pypi.org` reached the proxy only because the machine's resolver happened to answer from the machine's `/etc/hosts`: on dev-georgios, `systemd-resolved` on 127.0.0.53, reached through passt's `--dns-forward`. A machine whose resolver does not read `/etc/hosts` (a plain `nameserver` line, `ReadEtcHosts=no`), and every ns slot on a private network, which is given only nameservers off the loopback, resolved the registries to their real addresses and went around the proxy. Nothing in `~/nc-live` on dev-georgios changed this: the runner scripts pass `--slot-forward 127.77.0.1:443` and `--ca-bundle`, and the mapping came from the machine's stub resolver.

**What changed.** `sandbox/slot.sh` setup writes `rt/krun/hosts`: the lines of the machine's `/etc/hosts` whose address is the address of a forward or its IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (`::ffff:127.77.0.1`), comments dropped, empty without forwards. The krun guest (`krun/guest/src/boot.rs`, used by krun slots and by ns slots) appends that file, read from `/opt/nanoeval/krun/hosts`, to the `/etc/hosts` it writes. `NANOEVAL_SLOT_FORWARD` is part of what a finished setup was asked for, so a setup for other forwards runs again. Image builds keep their own `/etc/hosts` and are unchanged.

**Checked.** On dev-georgios (32 cores, KVM, the AEGIS block of `/etc/hosts` mapping 12 registry names to 127.77.0.1), one krun slot on a private network from `python:3.12-alpine`, with `NANOEVAL_SLOT_FORWARD=127.77.0.1:443` and the machine's CA bundle, by a script on `Sandboxd` and `Slot` (one run each):

| | Before: main's `slot.sh` and the deployed launcher | After |
|---|---|---|
| `pypi.org` lines in the guest's `/etc/hosts` | 0 | 2 |
| `getent hosts pypi.org` | `::ffff:127.77.0.1`, by DNS | `::ffff:127.77.0.1`, from the file |
| GET `https://pypi.org/simple/six/` | 200 | 200 |
| The same with the guest's resolver set to 192.0.2.1 | unresolved, `URLError [Errno -3]` | 200 |

`test/Sandbox.test.ts` holds the file a setup writes for two forwards against the machine's `/etc/hosts`, that a setup without forwards writes it empty and that a forward off the loopback is refused (it fails on main's `slot.sh`: no `rt/krun/hosts`), and the krun microVM test reads the guest's `/etc/hosts`. `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`, `npm test` (255 tests, the krun ones not skipped), `npm run dry-run`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, and the krun lanes `NANOEVAL_E2E_SCENARIO=network` (4 of 4) and `closed` (3 of 3) passed. The ns lanes need root and were not run.

**Release.** The guest is part of the launcher, so a runner machine takes it when its `NANOEVAL_KRUN` binaries are rebuilt from this commit (dev-georgios runs prebuilt ones from `~/nc-live/krunfull`). A new `slot.sh` with an old guest writes the file and the guest ignores it, as before. The Worker, nanocode-ts and the hand are unchanged.


## 2026-11-14: a verifier that could not install what its test.sh installs, read for why

Runs on dev-georgios (krun, private network): `a763f96d` (`rest-codex-retry`, a rerun of the 25 errored attempts of `bec3e408` `rest-codex-plan2`) ended 5 passed, 3 failed, 17 errored, and every one of the 17 was a `verifier` error, "the verifier wrote reward 0 without the test report its test.sh names". So were all 25 errors of `bec3e408`, 4 of `200a4c68` (`claude-full`), and 8 of the gate runs `8feaf3f8` and `8999a51d` (E2B, ns slots). 58 attempts in all, read one by one from their `verifier/test-stdout.txt` and the runner logs. None was the harness or the agent:

| Cause | Attempts | Tasks | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| The Debian archive withdrew the package | 28 | `qemu-alpine-ssh`, `qemu-startup` | `apt-get install curl` gets `404 Not Found` for `curl 7.74.0-1.3+deb11u16` from `deb.debian.org/debian-security`. The same URL answers 404 from the machine itself, `dists/bullseye-security/InRelease` is dated 2026-09-12, and `archive.debian.org` serves the file (200): Debian 11's security pool left the mirror after the end of its LTS. Known since the entry of 2026-11-10 |
| A download in the slot stalled for 30 s | 22 | `torch-pipeline-parallelism`, `torch-tensor-parallelism`, `mteb-retrieve`, `pytorch-model-recovery`, `gpt2-codegolf` | uv: "Failed to download distribution due to network timeout" on 150 to 825 MB wheels from the registry proxy behind `--slot-forward`; curl: "(56) Recv failure: Connection timed out" fetching the uv installer. The machine pulls the same torch 2.7.0 wheel through the same proxy, 865 MB, in 7.1 s. In `a763f96d` 5 of the 12 attempts of these tasks failed this way again and 7 ran their tests |
| The slot's disk failed | 2 | `sam-cell-seg`, `feal-differential-cryptanalysis` | `Input/output error (os error 5)` from uv and dpkg, in the E2B gate runs, which also had 12 `No space left on device` failures of agents |
| The disk of the sandbox filled under the launcher | 6 | `reshard-c4-data`, `sam-cell-seg`, `feal-differential-cryptanalysis` | "the verifier exited with 101 and wrote no reward", in the same E2B gate runs. Each log ends mid-line at a multiple of 4,096 bytes (4,096, 16,384, 36,864), one after `test_outputs.py .........  [100%]`. 101 is a Rust panic: when the output of `nanoeval-krun exec` cannot be written its error path calls `eprintln!`, which panics when stderr is on the same full disk. A two-line program that does the same exits 101 with stdout and stderr on `/dev/full` and 0 with stderr elsewhere |

**What changed.** `src/Verdict.ts` reads a verifier that did not run its tests (no reward, or a reward other than 1 without its report) for why, in the last 2,000 characters of its log, which the message already carries, and in `diskMb`, the least free disk of the filesystems of the slots that the runner saw while the verifier ran (`sandbox/Runner.ts` samples it at each poll of the verify phase, with the `statfs` the free-disk floor uses). Less than 1 MB free or `No space left on device` ends as `environment` "the slot ran out of disk while the verifier ran", `Input/output error` as `environment` "the disk of the slot failed while the verifier ran", and uv's `network timeout`, curl's transport errors 6, 7, 28, 35, 52 and 56, `Temporary failure resolving`, `Could not resolve host`, `Connection timed out`, `Connection reset by peer` and `Read timed out` as `environment` "the verifier could not download what its test.sh installs". `src/Retry.ts` retries each of the three once as a lost claim, as it retries the other failures of a machine, so a stall that does not come back costs one attempt and not a sample. An apt line `E: Failed to fetch URL 404 Not Found` stays a `verifier` error, now "the verifier could not install what its test.sh installs: its package archive answered 404 Not Found", and is not retried: no machine can install that package. A verifier whose tests ran is scored as before, whatever its log and the disk say.

**Checked.** `test/Verdict.test.ts` holds the four cases with lines from the logs above, and failed 3 of its 4 tests on the code before this change. `output/replay.ts` (not committed) fed the real logs and verifier files of all 58 attempts to the verdict before and after: before, 58 `verifier` errors; after, 28 `verifier` errors that name the withdrawn package, 22 `environment` errors retried as "the verifier could not download its dependencies", 2 retried as "the disk of the slot failed", and the 6 exits with 101 unchanged, since those runs reported no free disk: a runner from this commit reports it. `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`, `npm test` and `npm run dry-run` pass; the directory lanes default, `failures` and `disk` pass (the default lane failed once on the timing of a 12 s cell at load average 61 and passed twice after, and on the commit before).

**Not done.** The 30 s stalls are in the slot's way to the proxy, the guest's forward over vsock and the relay, not in the proxy: that is where to look next, and `run --verifier-cache` already keeps what uv downloads per task. `nanoeval-krun` should not panic when its output cannot be written. The retry needs the Worker of this commit, and `diskMb` a runtime built from it.


## 2026-11-14: sessions send one request per model call

`worker/Sessions.ts` passes `hedge: { cap_percent: 0 }` to `App.create`, and `package.json` moves from build-281c7dd to build-67dea25 (nanocode-ts 67dea25, the same nanocode a5d401e0c and WASM build), whose `App.create` takes `hedge`. Since nanocode-ts c1fe48c a session that names no hedge policy hedges a model request whose first byte is later than max(1.5 s, the model's p90) with one duplicate, up to 10% of the isolate's recent requests, and `App` named none, so every nanoeval session hedged. In run 16e15f9a (build-281c7dd, gpt-6-luna, nanox and nanoxd, 439 model calls) the `model.call.completed` events carry 47 dispatched hedges, of which the duplicate won 4, and 49 capped ones; each dispatched hedge resent the whole input on a second connection, 1,205,127 input tokens beside the 11,954,285 of the calls (10.1%), which the session's `cost_usd` counts and the ChatGPT plan pays. Run 0d6c29c9 (104 calls) has 10 hedges and 7.4%. An attempt's tokens and `modelCalls` come from the winners' `model.call.completed` events and were not inflated, but its cost and the model endpoint's requests were, and codex-cli and claude-code send one request per call. With the cap at 0 no duplicate is sent.

The end-to-end test takes `NANOEVAL_E2E_FIRST_BYTE_MS`: the scripted model holds each reply that long, and the run must then have sent the model endpoint exactly one request for each model call of its attempts. CI runs the directory-slot lane with 2000 ms.

Measured on dev-georgios (32 cores, Node 24.22.2), `NANOEVAL_E2E_BACKEND=dir NANOEVAL_E2E_FIRST_BYTE_MS=2000`, tasks extract-todos, uppercase-message and write-greeting, 3 slots, 1 attempt, one run each:

- before (bf18082, build-281c7dd): the scripted model got 18 requests for 12 model calls, and the assertion failed; the hedged `wrong` agent's cost was $0.0006 against $0.0005 with no hedge.
- after (this change, build-67dea25): 12 requests for 12 model calls, `e2e passed: scripted-dir`, `wrong` $0.0005, `right` $0.0002 in both.

Checked: `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`.

## 2026-11-14: a runner admits what its control group allows, its microVMs run in scopes of their own, and it frees disk below the floor

**What broke.** Run `650d0782` on dev-georgios ran in the systemd user unit `nc-losers` with `MemoryMax=12G`. Its runner admitted 80 % of the machine's 62 GB, so three `mcmc-sampling-stan` rows of the run compiled RStan at once, the unit reached its limit, and the kernel killed in the unit: the runner stopped with it and the run waited for a restart by hand. The units that run now (`nc-claude`, `nc-losers3`, `nc-ab`) have `MemoryMax` of 16 to 26 GiB, `OOMPolicy=stop` and `KillMode=control-group`, and every microVM of theirs ran inside the unit with `oom_score_adj` 200, the same as the runner: any kill for memory in the unit stops the whole unit. Separately, the cache of the machine held 89 unpacked disks (534 files, 50 GB) and 268 blobs (19 GB) that no run removed: `--free-disk-mb` held back claims, and only `--disks remove` removed anything, and only disks that the same run had unpacked. Finished one-run homes under `output/runners` kept their runtime, 600 MB each (24 homes, 11 GB).

**The rules.**

- **A runner's memory is what it may use.** `sandbox/Memory.ts` reads the runner's control group from `/proc/self/cgroup` and the `memory.max` of it and of every group above it. The capability `memory_mb` that the runner reports, and so the 80 % it admits, is the lower of the machine's memory and the tightest of those limits. A row that asks for more than the runner admits gets what is free as before, now the lower of `MemAvailable` and the headroom of the tightest group (`memory.max` less what it uses beyond page cache). `--memory-mb` still overrides it. A runner in no limited group sees no change.
- **Each microVM runs in a systemd scope of its own.** Setup of a krun home asks the user manager for a scope once (`systemd-run --user --scope true`) and writes `scope` in the home when it answers. Then `slot.sh` starts each microVM as `nanoeval-slot-KEY.scope` with `MemoryMax` of its guest memory and 256 MiB more and `MemorySwapMax=0`, by exec, so `vm.pid` is still the microVM. Its memory no longer counts against the runner's unit, a kill for memory there ends that scope alone, and `gone` gives its row back to the run as it does for any slot that ends under its row. Where no user manager answers, setup says so in its log and the microVM runs as before. Every slot process, krun or ns, has `oom_score_adj` 1000, the kernel's most, so that a kill for memory on the machine takes a slot before the runner, its Worker or other services.
- **The 256 MiB** are measured: on dev-georgios a guest that filled its memory (`head -c 6000m /dev/zero | tail -n 1`, killed by the guest's kernel) took the launcher's resident set 12 MiB over the guest at one vCPU and 31 to 32 MiB over at four, for 512 and 2,048 MiB guests; `passt` of a private network adds about 34 MiB. 256 MiB is four times the most measured.
- **Below `--free-disk-mb` a runner frees disk, with either `--disks`.** First, with `--disks remove`, the disks that its run unpacked and none of its rows uses, as before. Then `Disks.collect` removes cached disks, blobs and partial downloads of processes that are gone, the least recently used first, while the cache's filesystem is below the floor. It keeps every blob of every row the runner holds, the disks of the rows that the run said come next (`ahead`) and disks being unpacked. A disk goes through `slot.sh drop`, which takes the disk's lock exclusively without waiting, so a disk that a slot of any runner on the machine boots stays, and its `.use`, `.lock` and every `.run-*` mark go with it. A disk's last use is the later of its file and its `.workdir`, which the runner writes each time a row starts on it; a blob's is its modification time, which `Store.ensure` now sets when it finds the blob cached. Disks that other runs unpacked were never removed before; the disk lane now asks that they are.
- **A one-run runner removes its runtime when its run is finished.** When it leaves a finished run, holds no row and stands in no pool, it removes `rt`, `setup.for` and `setup.status` from its home, so a runner started there again sets up again.

**Checked** on dev-georgios (32 cores, 62 GB, kernel 6.8, systemd 255, Node 24.22.2), at a load average of 55 to 65 from the three runs above, with the krun binaries those runs use.

- **Before and after, one row that fills 2 GiB of guest memory** (a local task, `memory_mb = 2048`, whose solution runs `{ head -c 1980m /dev/zero; sleep 15; } | tail -n 1`), the krun oracle lane run inside `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=2560M -p MemorySwapMax=0`, a stand-in for a runner unit with `OOMPolicy=stop`:
  - On `6c755ac`: the microVM ran in the lane's scope with `oom_score_adj` 200; 23 s after the start, at 1,367 MB of microVM, systemd logged "A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer" and stopped the scope: the lane, its Worker and its runner ended with 143.
  - With the change: the microVM ran in `nanoeval-slot-….scope` with `memory.max` 2,415,919,104 (2,048 + 256 MiB) and `oom_score_adj` 1000, reached 2,061 MB, and the lane passed in 48 s (1 passed, the guest's own kernel counted one OOM kill).
  - `Memory.limit` inside such a scope read `{"limitMb":2560,"headroomMb":2537}`, and in a login shell nothing.
- `test/Memory.test.ts` (a unit's `MemoryMax`, the tightest group above it, no limit) and `test/Disks.test.ts` (order by last use without held digests, removal until the floor, partial downloads of live processes kept, and `slot.sh drop` keeping a disk whose lock a slot holds while it removes the rest).
- `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`, `npm test` and `npm run dry-run`, and the krun lanes listed in the commit.

**Not verified.** A runner under one of the live units: they were not restarted. The scope on a machine whose user manager has no memory controller delegated, where `MemoryMax` of the scope is accepted and not enforced. A disk removed by one runner between another runner's unpack and the start of its slot, which is possible only for the newest disk of the cache.
## 2026-11-14: a builder guest that stops reading its layer is knocked, and a conversion that stalls is made again

**The defect.** The import of the Terminal-Bench gate on dev-georgios stopped three times on 2026-11-13 (`sqlite-db-truncate`, `mteb-retrieve` for 33 minutes, `qemu-alpine-ssh` for 23 minutes), with the signature of [the stall](#2026-11-13-the-two-entries-above-on-a-machine-with-kvm-and-a-stall-in-libkrun-that-is-open): the launcher's sending thread in `sock_alloc_send_pskb` on `vm.sock`, its reading thread in `unix_stream_data_wait`, every thread of the microVM asleep. Nothing in nanoeval bounded it: `Machine::request` wrote the layer with blocking writes and no timeout, and `Converter.convert` waited for the launcher without one, so an import that met it waited forever.

**Why it still happened after the pin of `8ce363e`.** The launcher that the machine's runners and imports use is not built from this repository's lock. `~/nc-live/krunfull/nanoeval-krun`, which `NANOEVAL_KRUN` names there and which `slot.sh tools` copied into the converter's `rt/krun`, holds the source paths of `libkrun-68c139de8acad8bb/df85b8b`: it was built from a checkout whose lock still named `containers/libkrun` at `df85b8b`, without the credit request interrupt. A launcher built from this lock holds `libkrun-508ca49eaab03505/8ce363e`.

**Reproduced** on dev-georgios (32 cores, load average 55 to 86 from other work), converting `alexgshaw/mteb-retrieve:20260430` (9 layers, 629 MB, cached) with `nanoeval-krun image build` four at a time, arms interleaved, a conversion counted as stalled when its directory and the layer cache did not change for 120 s:

| Launcher | Conversions | Stalled | Knocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `krunfull` (libkrun `df85b8b`, before this change) | 32 | 10 | none |
| libkrun `df85b8b` with this change | 12 | 0 | 2 conversions knocked once each, 35 and 40 s |
| libkrun `8ce363e` with this change | 20 | 0 | none |

A stall of the `krunfull` launcher, left at layer 5 of 9 for nine minutes, went on within three seconds of one `nanoeval-krun ready` against its socket and finished: a new connection is the wakeup that the stream lost, as the entry on the stall found.

**The rule.** The launcher bounds what it waits for, in `krun/host/src/image/machine.rs`. While it streams input to the builder guest, its socket has a write timeout of 10 s. A write that moves nothing in that time opens a second connection and pings the guest, which recovers a lost wakeup at once, and says so on stderr. A ping that is not answered within 10 s, or 30 knocks in a row that move nothing (5 min), end the request with "the builder guest read nothing of its input", and the launcher exits with 75 (`EX_TEMPFAIL`) instead of 125. `Converter.convert` makes a conversion that ended with 75 once more, with a fresh microVM, and logs why; a second stall, or any other failure, is the error it was. 10 s is above every write of the table that moved: with `8ce363e`, 20 conversions under that load had no write that waited 10 s. Other requests and slots are unchanged.

**Not changed here.** libkrun: the knock recovers its lost wakeup whatever its cause, and `8ce363e` removed every stall of the table. `krunfull` on dev-georgios is not replaced while runners use it: launchers built from this commit's lock (host, and guest and relay for musl) are left beside it.

**Checked** on dev-georgios: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` (51 tests, the two integration tests of the launcher run), three of them new: a guest that reads only once knocked gets all of 8 MiB, a guest that never reads ends as a stall after the limit, a guest that does not answer the knock ends as a stall. `test/Converter.test.ts` is new: the launcher's 75 is a `Converter.StalledError` and 125 is not, a conversion that stalled runs once more and logs it, and one that stalls twice or fails otherwise is not run again. `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`, `npm test` (257 tests, none skipped).

**Not verified.** CI on GitHub, and the end-to-end lanes beyond the plain krun lane.

## 2026-11-14: OpenMP in a microVM or ns slot runs no more threads than the slot has vCPUs

**The defect.** Terminal-Bench 2.1 `extract-moves-from-video` declares `cpus = 1`, so its krun slot has one vCPU, as [the resources](DESIGN.md) say. An agent there OCRs frames with tesseract 5.3.4 from Ubuntu 24.04, which links libgomp and asks for 4 threads in its LSTM loops (`num_threads` in the pragma), whatever `nproc` says. On one vCPU those threads take turns and spin, and recognition is about four times slower than with one thread. The microVM itself is not slower: one thread costs the same in the guest as on the host.

**Measured** on dev-georgios (AMD EPYC 4585PX, 32 cores, load average 47 to 89 from the live runners), one 1280x720 frame of 18 lines of text, the disk of `alexgshaw/extract-moves-from-video:20260403` on a krun slot of the runner's launcher, tesseract installed with apt in the slot, one run each unless counted:

| Where | Default | `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1` | `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=4` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| krun slot, 1 vCPU | 8.9 s | 2.0 and 2.2 s | 7.9 s |
| host, all 32 cores | 2.3 and 2.4 s | 2.1 and 2.1 s | |
| host, `taskset -c 5` | 6.5 and 6.2 s | 2.0 and 2.0 s | |

The guest sees one CPU with AVX2, AVX-512 and FMA, and tesseract reports AVX512BW, so no instruction set is missing. `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE` alone took 4.9 s.

**The rule.** `slot.sh` writes `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=<vCPUs>` to the slot's `cpus.env` when it brings up a krun or ns slot, and every command it runs in the guest (hand, agent, solution, verifier) reads that file before the image's environment, so an image or `NANOEVAL_SLOT_ENV` that sets the variable keeps its own value. The slot's vCPUs stay the task's `cpus` rounded up. A directory slot is unchanged: it has no CPU limit.

**Before and after**, the same six frames three times through `slot.sh _solve` on a 1-vCPU krun slot of that disk, the slot brought up by the script of `7cad077`/`daf5fdb` and by this one: 58.7, 49.8 and 53.6 s before, with `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT` unset; 12.3, 12.6 and 13.5 s after, with `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1`.

**Checked** on dev-georgios: the krun lane of `test/Sandbox.test.ts` asserts that a solution in a 1-vCPU slot sees `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1`, and fails with the script before this change. `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types`, `npm test`.

**Not verified.** An attempt of the task with a model on these slots, and the ns backend, which takes the same file through the same `exec`.


## 2026-11-14: `nanoeval-krun` and `nanoeval-net` do not panic when stderr cannot be written

**The defect.** Six verifier errors of the E2B gate runs (entry "a verifier that could not install what its test.sh installs") were `nanoeval-krun exec` exiting 101 with its log cut at a multiple of 4,096 bytes: the disk under its output was full, its error path called `eprintln!`, and `eprintln!` panics when the write to stderr fails. On dev-georgios, with stderr on `/dev/full`, the deployed `nanoeval-krun bogus` and `nanoeval-net bogus` both exited 101 instead of reporting the usage error with 125.

**The rule.** The two host binaries write their diagnostics with an `eprintln!` of their own, defined in `krun/host/src/main.rs` and exported by `krun/net/src/lib.rs`, which writes to stderr and drops a write error: a diagnostic that cannot be written is lost, and the exit code still says what happened. Every existing call site keeps its text. Output that is data, `println!` and the streams of `exec`, is unchanged and still fails when it cannot be written. The guest binary writes to the console of its microVM and is unchanged.

**Checked** on dev-georgios: `krun/host/tests/stderr.rs` and `krun/net/tests/stderr.rs` run each binary with an unknown command and stderr on `/dev/full` and expect 125; the deployed binaries of `~/nc-live/runner/rt` exit 101 the same way. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` in `krun/`.

**Release.** A runner machine takes it when its `NANOEVAL_KRUN` binaries are rebuilt from this commit.
