Whether `auth.openai.com` takes the request without `refresh_reason` from this client is taken from nanocode-egress, which sends it so, and from releases of Codex before the field; whether `platform.claude.com` takes a refresh with the scopes of the file is taken from the fallback of Claude Code. ## 2026-11-14: the model calls of a subagent are counted, and its steps are a trajectory under its session

A session can start subagents, and `Atif` read the events of the session's own agent only. The entry on the tool call that a session publishes again named it: 4 calls counted for 9 answered. This entry counts them, puts the steps of a subagent into the trajectory, and adds the lane that checks the usage of such a session against its model endpoint. It changes `src/Atif.ts`, `test/Subagent.test.ts` with its recorded streams, `test/e2e.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, README.md and DESIGN.md.

**What was measured.** A lane with a scripted model (below) ran three sessions on nanocode-ts `build-f3aa94f` with the hand `nanocode-cli-d2473f9`, on directory slots: a `claude` session on `claude-haiku-5-5`, a `codex` session in Code Mode and one with direct tools, both on a model nanocode does not know. Each started one subagent, waited for it and ran one more command. The model endpoint answered 7 requests for each, 4 of the session and 3 of its subagent, and the scripted answers of a subagent carry other token counts than those of its session.

| Session | Before: calls, input (cached), output, cost | After | The endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude` | 4, 32 (0), 16, $0.0000112 | 7, 158 (36), 34, $0.00002956 | 7, 158 (36), 34 |
| `codex`, Code Mode | 4, 400 (160), 28 and 12 reasoning, $0 | 7, 580 (220), 55 and 27 reasoning, $0 | 7, 580 (220), 55 and 27 |
| `codex`, direct tools | the same | the same | the same |

The trajectory of each had the five steps of the session and nothing of the subagent. The `status` line of the agent, the comparison, the exported totals and the estimate of the spend are made from this usage, so each was short by the same part.

**How a subagent appears**, read in nanocode at `0e428f673` (`crates/runtime/agent/src/session_events.rs`, `one_log.rs`, `crates/runtime/subagents`) and in the recorded streams. The stream of a session carries events with the source `subagent` beside those with the source `agent`. Each has `root_session_id`, `detach` and an `update`:

- `added` with `agent`: the `id` of the subagent, a number that is unique in the session, its own `session_id`, its `role`, its `task`, the `parent` that started it (`null` for the session itself) and its model and thinking.
- `event` with `id`, `parent` and `event`: one event of the subagent's own agent, with `type` and `payload` as the session's events have them. A subagent accepts its task (`input.accepted`, the text nanocode wraps the task in), starts a run (`run.started` with its model), calls its model and its tools, and ends its run (`run.completed` or `run.failed`).
- `status`, `completion` and `message`, which say what state a subagent is in, what it returned and what was sent to it. `Atif` does not read them.

`model.call.completed` of a subagent is handed over without a place in the log, with the sequence number 0, as the session's is, and the table of the session object keeps it by the same rule: `Telemetry` does not ask whose call it is. The logged event of a subagent carries the id of the subagent's turn as its `request_id`, not the turn of the attempt, and `Harness.events` reads the events of the session whatever their turn.

Each agent reports its own usage when its run ends. The `run.completed` of the session above says 4 model calls, 400 input tokens and its own cost, and that of its subagent 3 calls, 180 tokens and its own cost: nothing in the session's event counts the subagent.

**The rule.**

- **Usage.** `Atif.usage` reads the events of every agent of a session by the rules it had for the session: a model call is counted at its `model.call.completed` unless it is marked `timing.replayed`, and a tool call at the first `tool.call` of its `call_id`, each for the agent that made it. The usage of an attempt is the sum: model calls, input, cached and cache write tokens, output and reasoning tokens, tool calls.
- **Cost.** The cost is the sum of the `cost_usd` that the runs of all its agents reported. It is not known, and `status` says so, while a model call of any agent is not followed by a run end of that agent that carries a cost: a subagent that still ran when the events were read, or a turn that was cancelled, whose `run.failed` has none. A sum over the agents that did report would be a cost that leaves out calls and looks whole. Where the endpoint charged for the responses of the row, the cost stays the sum of those charges, as before: every request of a subagent goes through the same endpoint under the session of its row.
- **Trajectory.** The steps of the session are what they were. Each subagent is a trajectory of its own in `subagent_trajectories`, which ATIF-v1.7 has for this, under the agent that started it, so a subagent of a subagent is under that one. It has the `trajectory_id` `agent-N`, the session id of the subagent, its model, and its id and role in `agent.extra`. The result of the `spawn_agent` call that started it carries `subagent_trajectory_ref` with that id. `final_metrics` of a trajectory counts its agent and every trajectory under it, as Harbor's own agents with subagents do, `notes` says so, `extra.subagents` is how many are directly under it, and `total_steps` stays the number of steps of that agent, which ATIF asks for. A subagent that published no step is counted and has no trajectory: Harbor refuses a trajectory without steps.
- **One step for each model call.** Three orders of events broke it once a subagent was there, and all three were in the session's own steps too. A `codex` session publishes the message of a reply before the `model.call.completed` of that reply, so the message went to the step of the call before, and after an input that was accepted in the middle of a turn it made a step without a model call. A message now waits for the call its `model_call_index` names. And the result of a tool call that arrived after such an input made a step of its own: it now goes to the step that made the call, which is also what Harbor's models ask of an observation. And a tool call that is published for the first time after such an input made a step of its own, as the command inside a cell does when the Worker was killed between the cell and its command: what an agent publishes while no step of its own is open now goes to the step of its latest model call.

**After the Worker was killed, on `build-f3aa94f`**, which does not have nanocode-ts's change for a turn with subagents that goes on. One run of each kill, three sessions each:

- **Killed while the cell of the subagent runs.** The stream then holds `added` and `status` of the subagent again, its task accepted again under the same `request_id`, `run.started` again, its first model call again marked `timing.replayed`, a `message` and an input of the kind `steer` that tells the subagent its runtime restarted, and the result of its cell with the status `unknown`. The session's own events repeat as the earlier entries say, its `wait_agent` fails, and it later accepts "Subagent 1 completed" as an input of its own. All three rows passed. Counted and answered: 7 and 7 for `claude` and for Code Mode, 8 and 8 for direct tools, whose model was asked once more.
- **Killed after the subagent ended, while the last command of the session runs.** `added` and `completion` come again. `claude` and Code Mode: 7 and 7. The session with direct tools was given a turn of its own after the turn of the attempt had its result, `subagent-completion:<session of the subagent>:1`, with one model call: 8 and 8, and that turn is a user step and an agent step at the end of its trajectory.

In all six the usage is what the endpoint answered, each replayed call is counted once, and every agent step has its model call. Before the two rules above the same streams gave 9 agent steps for 8 and for 7 calls.

**After the Worker was killed, on `build-b8158fd`**, the pin of this commit, which has that change. A `claude` session, three runs of each kill, and the stream of the first of each read:

- **Killed while the cell of the subagent runs.** The turn goes on where it was: the model of the session and the model of the subagent are each asked every request once, 7 requests, as without a kill. The stream holds `added` and `status` again, the task accepted again, the first model call of the subagent marked `timing.replayed`, and the `tool.call` of its cell and of the command inside it a second time, unmarked, with one result each. A notice that its runtime restarted is still sent to the subagent as an input of the kind `steer`, which is a user step in its trajectory. Usage, cost and the totals of the trajectory are those of the run without a kill, to the tool call.
- **Killed after the subagent ended.** Nothing of the subagent is published again, the session's own model call comes again marked, and the turn ends as without a kill.

In the fourth run with the kill in the cell, the Worker went down after the `tool.call` of the cell and before the `tool.call` of the command inside it. That call then came for the first time after the notice of the restart, and the lane failed on its count of steps, 8 for the 7 model calls of a row that had passed with the right usage. The third rule above is from that stream.

**What each kind of agent counts, and what it cannot see.**

- **A `claude` session.** Counted from the events: the model calls, tokens and tool calls of the session and of every subagent under it, a Code Mode cell and each call inside it as tool calls. Not seen: a response that never became a model call, because the Worker was killed as it arrived or because the attempt of a call failed and was asked again (the endpoint has it in `agent/model-requests.jsonl`, with its cost where it charged one); a model call in flight when the turn is cancelled; reasoning tokens, which a Claude response does not report; and what a subagent does after the events of the row were read, which is when its session is deleted. A subagent on another model is counted and priced by nanocode at its own prices, and the summary shows the sum under the one model of the agent: each step of the trajectory names its model.
- **A `codex` session, in Code Mode or with direct tools.** Since the entry of this day on codex sessions without web search and subagents, its turn carries `subagents: false`, so it starts none and its usage is its own model calls. The lane `direct` now asks that no request of either session declares `spawn_agent`. On a Worker of a build before `build-b8158fd` the field is ignored, a codex session has the subagent tools, and they are counted as a `claude` session's are: the recorded streams of `build-f3aa94f` are of that case. A session on a plan login over the WebSocket is counted from its events though the endpoint does not meter it, as before. Not seen: as for `claude` without the line on reasoning, and whether a compaction is published as a model call was not looked at.
- **`claude-code`.** Not counted from its stream but at the model endpoint of the run: every answered `v1/messages` request that carried the token of the row, so those of its Task subagents, its title and summary requests and retries are all in the model calls and tokens. The cost is what the endpoint charged when every one of them carried a charge, else the `total_cost_usd` Claude Code prints. Tool calls are the `tool_use` blocks of its stream. Not seen: a response whose stream was cut before its usage, which is no call and no tokens here whatever the provider charged; `count_tokens` requests, which generate nothing. Its trajectory is the steps of the stream in one list, a subagent's among them and not marked.
- **`codex-cli`.** The same meter, on `responses` and `responses/compact`. `codex exec` as nanoeval runs it has no tool that starts another agent. Tool calls are the completed items of its stream. It prints no cost, so on a plan or a provider's own key it has tokens and none.

**The lane.** `NANOEVAL_E2E_SCENARIO=subagent`, on directory slots: one row of `write-greeting` for a `claude` session on `claude-haiku-5-5` at low thinking. The scripted model tells a subagent from its session by the task, which only the subagent has as its prompt. The session is answered `spawn_agent`, `wait_agent` on the id it was given, a command that reads the file, and a final message, each in a cell. The subagent is answered a command that writes the greeting, `submit_result` and a final message, with 42 input tokens of which 12 are cached and 6 output tokens where the session has 8 and 4. It asks that the row passed, that the model calls of the row are the requests the endpoint answered, 7, with 158 input tokens of which 36 are cached, 34 output tokens and 10 tool calls, that the trajectory has the five steps of the session and under it one trajectory of four steps that begins with the task, named by the result of `spawn_agent`, with 7 and 3 model calls in their totals, and that the cost is the session's and the subagent's. The check of every lane, one agent step with its tokens for each model call and the tokens of the session those of the responses of its endpoint, now walks the trajectories under a trajectory and holds here. `NANOEVAL_E2E_KILL=child` kills the Worker five seconds after the subagent's command, which then sleeps twenty, wrote its mark, and `parent` does the same in the last command of the session: with a kill the lane asks the same of the requests and of the usage, that the claim of the row outlived the Worker, and not for the list of steps, since the notice of the restart is a step. All three are in `ci.yml`.

`claude-haiku-4-5`, the model of the other lanes, cannot start a subagent here: nanocode refuses one below low thinking, and that model has none.

**Rejected.**

- **The steps of a subagent in the list of its session, marked.** Harbor's models and viewers know `subagent_trajectories`, and a list of two agents' steps in the order they were published has no place for the tokens of one agent's context beside the other's. A reader that wants one list has the timestamps.
- **A field of `Usage` for what the subagents spent.** The trajectory has it for each subagent. The summary, the comparison and the budget ask what a row cost, which is the sum.
- **The usage of a session with subagents taken from the endpoint.** The reasons of the entry on the model calls a log no longer holds stand: a WebSocket is not metered, and a response is not a model call.

**Checked** on a Linux x86_64 machine with 5 cores and no KVM, beside the lanes of other work, at a load average near 10. No model was paid for.

- `test/Subagent.test.ts`, nine tests on seven streams recorded by the lane as their `agent/events.jsonl`, cut only in the `timing` of a model call to the two fields the fixture of the earlier entry keeps, and with the path of the slot's workspace on the machine, which `run.started` carries on `build-b8158fd`, replaced by `/work`. Five are of `build-f3aa94f`: the three sessions without a kill, the `claude` session killed while its subagent's cell ran, and the session with direct tools killed after its subagent ended. Two are of `build-b8158fd`: the `claude` session killed while its subagent's cell ran, once after the command inside the cell was published and once before. They hold the usage of each against the sums of the scripted answers, the usage of the same stream without its subagent events, the trajectories step by step, the reference from `spawn_agent`, the totals of each trajectory, the message of a codex reply on the step of its call, a cost that is unknown without the run end of the subagent, the replayed call of a subagent counted once with every result in the step of its call, the calls of a subagent's cell that are published again counted once, with the usage and the totals of the run that was not killed, the command that is first published after the notice of a restart in the step of its model call, the turn a session is given when its subagent ends, and a subagent under a subagent, made from a recorded one. On `src/Atif.ts` as it was all nine fail.
- The events of 1,808 sessions that this machine holds from the lanes and runs of other work, 17 of them with a subagent, projected with `src/Atif.ts` as it was and as it is: the usage of the 1,791 without a subagent is the same in every field. Agent steps without a model call go from 302 to 2, both in sessions of a build whose log held no model call at all, and results that are not in the step of their call from 1,142 to 6, each the unknown outcome of a call that a kill cut before it was published. No session has more of either than before.
- `npm test`: 369 tests, 365 passed and 4 skipped, on the pins of this commit, nanocode-ts `build-b8158fd`, with the changes that landed beside this one. `npm run lint` and `npm run check:types` pass.
- The trajectories of the recorded runs on `build-f3aa94f`, three sessions without a kill and six with one, and of the four lanes on `build-b8158fd` below, load with the models of Harbor 0.25.0 (`scripts/harbor-check.py`, none refused).
- The lane on `build-f3aa94f` with the three sessions it then had: passed, 21 requests answered and counted, in a run of 10 s from its creation to the verdict.
- **On the pins of this commit**, `build-b8158fd` with the hand `nanocode-cli-0bbcb64`, each lane through one of the two lane slots of the machine, after a wait of forty minutes for the first. Before the third rule: the lane without a kill passed 3 times of 3, with the kill after the subagent ended 4 times of 4, the Worker back after 3.1 to 6.0 s, and with the kill in the subagent's cell 3 times of 4, back after 2.8 to 4.4 s, the fourth being the run described above. With the third rule the kill in the cell passed 2 times of 2 and the kill after the subagent ended once. The first run of each kill was with the lane as it then was, which asked a killed turn only for the count of its model calls, and the others with the lane of this commit. In every run the models were asked `spawn_agent`, `wait_agent`, `exec_command` and the final message, and `exec_command`, `submit_result` and the final message, each once. The lane `direct` passed 2 times of 2 with its new line: the session with direct tools was given `exec_command`, `write_stdin`, `view_image` and `hands`, and the one in Code Mode `exec` and `wait`. The lanes whose shared check of the steps changed passed once each before the third rule: the plain lane with three tasks, the kills in a cell, in a wait and of a pair, and the restart.

**Not verified.**

- A real model, a deployed Worker, krun and ns slots. The change is in what the Worker makes of events and no slot sees it.
- A session whose subagent is on another model or provider, a subagent that starts a subagent in a real session, and a subagent that is still running when its session's turn ends: the rules were read against the event shapes and the last two are unit tested on made streams only.
- `claude-code` and `codex-cli` with a subagent of their own: what is said of them above is read in `worker/Run.ts`, `src/Proxy.ts` and `src/Installed.ts`, and no installed agent was run with one.
- A second `tool.result` for one `call_id` is still two results, now in the step of the call.
- CI on GitHub.

## 2026-11-14: a session that is refused its model does not hold its slot to its agent timeout

**The defect.** On the pins of main since 11:00 UTC, nanocode-ts `build-b8158fd` with the hand `nanocode-cli-0bbcb64`, the lane whose key is spent during the run failed, on main alone as on these changes: the row that was running when the gateway began to answer `402 payment_failed` did not end as a `budget` error when the wait of the run was over. It ran to its agent timeout of 300 s, its verifier ran, and it was scored 0. On the pins before, `build-f3aa94f`, the lane passes.

**The cause is in nanocode.** nanocode 9bebe258c, "a 402 from the Tempo gateway's payment layer is retried like a server error", is in the SDK of `build-b8158fd` (0bbcb64a0) and not in that of `build-f3aa94f` (0e428f673). Its Claude client counts a `402` as transient when the problem type is `/reference#description/payment-failed`, `.../verification-failed` or `.../session/delta-too-small` (`crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs`, `TRANSIENT_PAYMENT_PROBLEMS` and `is_transient`), because the gateway answers that way when its payment layer is overloaded. The gateway answers the same type for a wallet that is empty, a spending limit that is used up and a key that is expired or revoked, and nothing in the body tells them apart. The session then asks 11 times, 500 ms doubling to 32 s with jitter, 184 s in all. The error that ends those attempts is still retryable, so the turn is not failed: the session object of nanocode-ts takes the turn for interrupted and runs it again from its start (`src/cloudflare/App.ts`, "runtime recovery required"), and so on with no end. Nothing but the agent timeout of the row ended it. A `codex` session is not affected: its client sends a refused request five more times, 0.2 s doubling, and fails the turn 6.2 s after it was handed the refusal, for 401, 402, 403, 404 and 422 alike. The fix for nanocode is one line, delivered beside these changes and not part of them: a 402 keeps its attempts and the error after the last one fails the turn. With that fix alone the row still asks for 184 s after the run has given up, so the run needs a rule of its own.

**What it cost.** A row that is refused holds its slot from the refusal to its agent timeout, and then its verifier runs: 300.0 s after the first refusal in the lane, where the wait of the run is 15 s. Its outcome is `failed` with reward 0 and not an error, so it counts against the agent in every rate and `--rerun --errored` leaves it out. For Terminal-Bench 2.1 the agent timeouts of the 89 tasks are 600 s to 12,000 s, 151,950 s in all and 1,707 s on average. Rows are claimed longest timeouts first, so with a key whose wallet is empty from the start a run of 16 slots starts the 16 longest, 68,400 s of agent timeouts: they hold their slots and the sandboxes under them for up to 12,000 s where the run would have ended after `--setup-sec`, 600 s, and 16 of the 89 tasks get a 0 that no model earned. With 8 slots it is 40,800 s, with 4 slots 26,400 s. A key that is spent in the middle of a run costs the rest of the timeout of every row that runs then. These are sums over the timeouts of the tasks and not a run: no run with a spent key was made at that size.

**What changed.** The run ends the turn itself, and the row ends as it did on `build-f3aa94f`.

- `Retry.refused` reads the model requests of the row's claim, without those of its judges, and takes the requests at the end that were answered 401, 402, 403 or 404, back to the last one that was answered anything else. These four say that the caller is not served, whatever it sends. 400, 413 and 422 are about one request, which a session may change, and 408, 409, 429 and 5xx pass: none of them counts.
- When the last of them is a refusal for a spent key and the wait of the run for the payment is over (`--setup-sec` after the first refusal, the rule that already ends the rows not yet started), the row ends at once as a `budget` error: "the run ended the turn: its model request was answered 402 after the payment was refused for 600 s", with what the gateway said.
- Otherwise, when those requests span `--setup-sec` or more from the first to the last, the row ends as an `agent` error that names how many they were and their statuses. One refusal alone ends nothing, however old it is: a turn that asks nothing more may be in a long tool call.
- The run reads this with every `agent` call of the runner while the turn runs, before the agent timeout, and the relay wakes that call when it hands a refusal to the session instead of sending the request again. The failure is written to the row before the turn is cancelled, so a call that is repeated answers the same.
- No limit is new: the wait is `--setup-sec`, which a run already waits for a payment, for a runner and for a sandbox.

**What was considered and not done.** Counting N refusals in a row: the relay sends a refused request again itself, so a count would have to tell its tries from the session's, and it would need a number that nothing gives. Reading the detail of the gateway to tell an empty wallet from an overload: the texts are prose and change. Ending the row when the session's own turn fails, as before, stays the first thing the run reads, so a build that ends its turn keeps its own message.

## 2026-11-14: what a second reading of the day's changes found, and its fixes

The changes that the entry above lists were read once more after they were proven: `cli/Login.ts` and what calls it, `src/Atif.ts`, `cli/Doctor.ts`, the refusals of the command line and the quick start. Six defects and one sentence of the README came out of it. None changes what a run scores; one changes what a run is said to have cost.

**A login file that root refreshes stays with its owner.** `nanoeval doctor` tells the operator of ns slots to run the runner or the revision as root, with `sudo -E`. A refresh made that way replaced the login file by one that root owns, mode 600, and made the lock files beside it as root: the tool of the owner could then read neither its login nor its lock, and a watcher of that user could not take the lock of nanoeval again, so its token was never refreshed after that. The file that replaces a login takes the owner and the group of the file it replaces, and a lock file that nanoeval makes takes those of its directory. Only root can differ from them, so nothing changes for any other user.

**New tokens that could not be written are kept.** Both providers end a refresh token when they answer a refresh with a new one. When the write of the answer failed, a full disk or the write lock of Claude Code held past its 15 s, the answer was dropped and the line said `was not refreshed ... it is used as it is`: the file then held a refresh token that was spent, so the next refresh, of nanoeval or of the owner's tool, was refused and the login was signed out with no line that said why. The write is tried three times, 500 ms apart. When it still fails, the command keeps the answer and writes it with its next request for that login instead of asking again, and its line says that the refresh token is spent and that a command which ends before that leaves a login to sign in again. A login file that changed meanwhile is taken as before. The three tries and the 500 ms come from no measurement: they cover a lock that another writer holds for a moment, and what they do not cover is the kept answer.

**The cost of a turn that is run again is counted once.** nanocode reports with each run end the cost of its request so far, and `src/Atif.ts` added every one: a turn that failed and was run again counted its earlier part again with each run. Recorded on 2026-11-12: the `codex` session of the row `install-windows-3.11__nano-codex__1`, whose turn was run five times, has run ends of $0.026212 after 46 model calls and four of $0.026648 after 47, and its usage said $0.132804. With this change the same events give $0.026648, computed before and after from its `agent/events.jsonl`. The cost of an agent is now the sum over its requests of the last cost that a run end of the request reported, and a request is the prompt the agent accepted last, so a subagent and a second prompt add their own. The figure is `final_metrics.total_cost_usd` of every trajectory, and it is the cost of the row, of the comparison and of the model budget wherever the model endpoint priced nothing, a key of the provider or a plan login. Where the endpoint prices the requests, the gateway, nothing changes.

**`no Worker answers` for an address written with `localhost`.** For `http://localhost:PORT` Node tries `::1` and `127.0.0.1`, and the cause of `fetch failed` is an `AggregateError` whose own message is empty: the line was `a request got no answer`, with no address and no next step, where the README promises both. The causes inside it are read, and a Worker named as `localhost` is the one that did not answer when one of them names `127.0.0.1` or `::1` at its port.

**`nanoeval doctor` counts a login file only where a command takes it.** It counted a login file at its default path, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` or `~/.codex/auth.json`, as a model credential "which nanoeval worker and nanoeval revision take from it". Neither does: `revision` takes a file from `--claude-login`, `--codex-login`, `NANOEVAL_CLAUDE_LOGIN` or `NANOEVAL_CODEX_LOGIN`, and `worker` from its options alone. On a machine where the tool is signed in and no key is set, doctor ended `ready` and the first revision was refused for want of a credential. A login file counts when its variable names it, and its line says that `revision` alone takes it from there.

**libkrunfw is found where the loader of the launcher finds it.** The check before a Dockerfile is converted asked `ldconfig -p` alone. The launcher loads the firmware with `dlopen`, which also searches `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and the default directories, so a library in a directory that `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` names, or copied to `/usr/lib64` without a later `ldconfig`, was refused with `libkrunfw.so.5 is not installed on this machine` although its microVMs start, where the import worked before the check. The library also counts when a file of that name is in a directory of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or in `/lib`, `/usr/lib`, `/lib64` or `/usr/lib64`.

**The README on what doctor checks.** "A bare machine" said that doctor checks every step of its list. Of the packages of step 1 it looks for passt alone, and it reports the launcher as ok with cargo: a machine without a compiler or `musl-tools` ends `ready for krun slots` and its first import fails at the link. The sentence names what is checked and what the first build then says.

**Checked.** On a machine with five cores and no KVM, on the pins of main, nanocode-ts `build-b8158fd` with the hand `nanocode-cli-0bbcb64`, from a fresh clone of the seven commits.

- `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types` and `npm run dry-run` passed. `npm test`: 374 tests, 369 passed and 5 skipped, the 4 that need KVM and the one that needs root.
- The unit tests of the fixes: the owner and group of a refreshed file and of its locks (as root only), new tokens of both files that could not be written and are written by the next request with nothing asked again, three run ends of one request and a second request, and the refusal for `localhost`.
- The cost of the recorded session, computed with `Atif.usage` on its events before and after: $0.132804 and $0.026648.
- Lanes on directory slots, each once, through one of the two lane slots of the machine at a load average of 1.4 to 4.7: the plain lane (27 s), the plan signed in on the Worker (35 s), the two lanes of login files (26 s and 27 s), the restart, the four kills in a turn, direct tools, the three lanes of a subagent, the two refusals of a payment, the key that is spent, the two model budgets and the web searches. All 21 passed.
- Not run with these fixes: the other 28 lanes on directory slots, the lanes on krun and ns slots, which the machine cannot run, and the two lanes of `nanoeval revision`. No fix is in what they exercise but the cost of a session, which every lane with a session reads.

**Not verified.**

- A refresh as root against a real login, and the watcher of the owner after it: the unit test of the owner and group runs as root only and was run once so, in the clone the fixes were written in.
- A write that fails for real, a full disk or Claude Code holding its write lock: the unit test fails the write by other means.
- That every release of nanocode reports the cost of a request so far with a run end. It is what the recorded session of 2026-11-12 shows and what the unit test pins; a release that reported the cost of one run alone would now be counted too low, and the lanes with a scripted model do not tell the two apart.
- `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `/usr/lib64` on a machine with KVM: the check was read against `dlopen(3)` and run on none.
- The line of the subagent lane that asks that no request declares `spawn_agent` cannot fail for the session in Code Mode, whose tools are called inside `exec`. It is not changed here.
## 2026-11-14: lanes that wait for an order of events, a port that is kept, and a served lab that gives up its lock

The closing entry of the changes before these, "what was run for the changes of this day before they landed", names four lanes and a unit test that failed on a slow or loaded machine, a port that two lanes could both take, and a hang of `nanoeval revision` beside a served lab whose cause was not found. A job of the workflow gets four shared CPUs on a hosted runner, so each was reproduced on purpose on the commit of that entry, `98a1542`, and then changed. Six of the seven were the lane's or the test's. The hang was the command's.

The machine of every measurement below, unless it names another: Linux with 5 cores and 14 GB, kernel 6.18.56, Node 24.22.1, no KVM, shared with other jobs, two lanes at a time. "Pinned" is `taskset` to two CPUs with two busy loops (`sh -c 'while :; do :; done'`) on the same two.

**Three lanes held a runner to a constant.** `--setup-sec` is one limit with three uses: a sandbox must have a runner that says hello within it, a runner must have set its machine up within it, and a row that no runner can take waits for it twice before it ends. "free disk floor" set it to 5 so that its rows end soon and "a runner whose sandbox ends before the rows could" to 4, and the lane of a gateway that sells no renewal leased sandboxes for 6 s. Pinned, on `98a1542`: "free disk floor" failed 3 times of 3 with `the runner did not start within 5 s`, "a runner whose sandbox ends before the rows could" 3 of 3 with `sandbox setup did not finish within 4 s` for the runner of its second run, and the lane without renewals was stopped after 300 s with sandbox after sandbox ending under a runner that had taken no row.

Each of the three now measures before it sets a limit. It runs the solutions of its tasks once on an attached runner with `--setup-sec 600` and reads two marks of that run's timeline, the hello of the runner and the first verdict, both counted from the creation of the run. Three times the first, rounded up to a second, is added to the 5 and the 4 s of `--setup-sec`, and three times the second to the 6 s of the lease. Pinned, a runner said hello after 4.1 to 8.4 s and ended its first row after 6.8 to 14.2 s in the 20 runs of the table below, so `--setup-sec` was 17 to 31 s and a lease 30 to 33 s. Three is the margin of the lane: a runner that starts three times slower than one measured seconds before, and more than the lane's own seconds slower, fails it.

The measurement is added to the constant and does not replace it, because the first form of this change replaced it and the machine with KVM showed what that costs. There a runner said hello after 0.7 s and ended a row after 0.9 s, the lease became 3 s, and of 359 sandboxes 24 finished a row before the lane failed after 504 s on a terminate that the gateway answered 404. With leases of 4 to 6 s the lane passed there 6 times in 26 to 46 s: a sandbox loses about 2.5 s before its first row on that machine whatever its lease, in the ticks of the run and the polls of the runner, and that is what the lane's own seconds were for.

- "free disk floor" is otherwise as it was: with a floor that no machine meets no row is claimed, every row ends as an error of the environment that names the free disk, and the runner removes the disk of its run that no row uses and no other.
- "a runner whose sandbox ends before the rows could" slept `--setup-sec` and a second before it started its first runner, so that the runner came after the time in which a sandbox takes a row that it can never finish. It now starts that runner when the run shows it as `lost` with `the runner never reported`, which is that moment as the run sees it. Its sandboxes ended after 60 and 120 s. A row of the lane may take 330 s and `--setup-sec`, and with a `--setup-sec` of 21 the rows that the first runner cannot take ended after 63 s, three seconds after its sandbox, so the runner never logged that it claims no more: both sandboxes now end one second before a row could. The end of the second sandbox was held against the creation of its run plus a second, and is now held between the creation of the run and the hello of its runner.
- The lane without renewals had 8 attempts of 3 tasks so that its rows outlast a sandbox on a fast machine. That was luck with any lease, and with a lease that follows the machine it stopped holding: on the machine with KVM one sandbox finished all 24 rows of 4 attempts inside a lease of 11 s, and inside one of 27 s that a slow measurement had given a fast run. The lane now makes what it means: its gateway leaves the fourth model request of the lane unanswered, as the lane of two leased sandboxes leaves one. That is the second request of the second row, which runs on the first sandbox that works, so that row is still running when the lease of its sandbox ends, goes back to the run and is finished on another sandbox, whatever the lease. The lane asks that at least two sandboxes after the first finished rows, and has 4 attempts. In the runs below 4 sandboxes did. A form between, in which the gateway answered nothing more until that first sandbox had ended, failed on the machine with KVM 2 times of 9: the run opens the next sandbox before a lease ends, the request of a row on that next sandbox was held as well and for good, and while the run deleted the session of that row with its request in flight, which took 8 s, it asked no renewal for the sandbox after it. Its step of the workflow keeps `NANOEVAL_E2E_SANDBOX_LEASE_SEC` at 6, which is now the part of the lease that no measurement adds to.

Two things were seen and left. A runner that the run has drained hears so with the answer to a claim, and a claim that the run holds is answered with it only when something releases the hold: in the lane that is the end of the run. And a run that deletes the session of a `codex` row whose model request is in flight did nothing else for 8 s on the machine with KVM, no renewal among it: with the 3 s in which these lanes renew a lease that is a missed renewal, with the 60 s of a run that is not a lane it is not.

**Two attached runners.** The lane starts two runners at once and asks that both finished rows, and on a machine where the second said hello late the first had finished all eight. Pinned, `98a1542` passed 3 times of 3, so the load alone did not show it. With the second runner started 20 s after the first, `98a1542` failed 2 of 2 on `both runners finished rows of the run`, 1 where it asks 2. The scripted model now answers nothing until a row of each runner is past its claim, as the lane of two leased sandboxes holds its model until a sandbox is busy. With the same 20 s it passed 2 of 2. The lane joined those that fail when their event did not happen.

**The port of a Worker.** A lane, and `nanoeval revision` for the Worker of a lab, bound port 0, read the number and closed the socket, and wrangler bound the number seconds later. The kernel gives a closed port to the next process that asks for one. The command now keeps the port: it is the local port of a connection that the command opens to a listener of its own and holds until the Worker has ended. The kernel hands a bound port to nobody who asks for port 0, and lets a server that sets `SO_REUSEADDR`, as workerd and Node do, listen on a port whose only other holder is an established connection. In a network namespace of its own, with every port of the range (32768 to 60999) asked for until none was left: the kept port was handed out 0 times in 28230 binds and a server listened on it meanwhile, and a port that was bound and closed 1 time in 28230. A lane that restarts its Worker keeps the port across the restart. The lane of `nanoeval revision` no longer chooses a port for the served lab: the command takes one and prints it.

**The lock of the lab in a test of the watcher.** The test started a process that takes the lock of the lab, went on as soon as anyone held that lock, and asked that the watcher finds the lab taken. The evaluation before leaves a child that holds the lock for a moment after it, which the watcher allows for. When that child was seen and the holder of the test was still starting, the watcher found the lab free, ran, and the test failed (once in 7 runs of `npm test` at a load average of 29 to 51 on the machine with 24 cores). With the child kept for 0.6 s and the holder started 2 s late, the test of `98a1542` failed on the same assertion with the same output. The holder now says when it holds the lock, and is ended as a process group and no longer by the name of its `sleep`: with the same two delays the test passed 5 times of 5.

**A served lab that left its Worker and its lock behind.** An evaluation beside `nanoeval revision --serve` once waited 50 minutes for the lock of the lab's Worker. The served lab held that lock and had a Worker of its own that answered `/health`, and had written no `worker.json`. One SIGTERM to the process group of `nanoeval worker` did not leave it running in any of 56 tries, 0.25 to 14 s after its start on one CPU beside two busy loops (the group was gone 0.3 to 0.95 s later), nor in the 19 of that entry. What did: the served lab reads `worker.wanted` every `--poll-ms` while its Worker starts, an evaluation wrote that file in place, and a read between the truncation and the write found it empty. The error left the function that starts the Worker without stopping the Worker and without freeing the lock, and the served lab, which then saw an evaluation that wants the lab, started nothing and freed nothing. With the file written empty while the Worker of a served lab starts, and whole 0.3 s later, `98a1542` 25 s on: `the lab has no Worker of its own: Unexpected end of JSON input` in its log, the lock held, the Worker alive and answering 200, no `worker.json`, which is the state that was found. Now `worker.wanted` and `worker.json` are written under another name and renamed, a file that still cannot be read is named in the error, and whatever ends the start of a Worker stops it and frees its lock: the same 25 s on, the lock is free and no Worker is left.

Stopping a Worker or a runner sent one SIGTERM to its process group and then waited for the exit of its first process without a limit. `nanoeval worker` passes the signal to wrangler's launcher, which passes it on and exits only when wrangler does, so the wait was as long as anything below chose. `revision` now takes `--stop-sec` (30): a group that has not stopped by then is killed and the command says so, and what a process that did stop left in its group is killed with it, so the kept port is not released under a workerd that outlived wrangler. 30 is thirty times the slowest stop of the 56.

## 2026-11-14: a status line that counted a sandbox still asked for, and checks that read a clock where an order was meant

The closing entries of the changes before these name what they left open: the lane of a provider that refuses sandboxes for a cap failed once in six runs on a loaded machine, four checks failed once each on a machine with KVM at a load average of 20 to 65 and passed alone, and one line of a lane could not fail for one of its two sessions. Each was read from its log, reproduced by hand where a load alone did not show it, and changed. One was the product's. What a first start from the README on a bare machine found is at the end.

The machine of every measurement below, unless it names another: Linux with 5 cores and 14 GB, kernel 6.18.56, Node 24.22.1, no KVM, shared with other jobs, two lanes at a time. "Pinned" is `taskset` to two CPUs with two busy loops (`sh -c 'while :; do :; done'`) on the same two. "By hand" is a change of a few lines that was made in a copy of the tree for one run and is in no commit.

**The status line counted a sandbox that was being asked for.** A run writes a sandbox as `creating` before it asks its provider for it, so that a create whose answer is lost is known. The line of `status` about refused sandboxes counted that row as open: while a refused create was asked again it read `sandboxes: 2 open; another could not be opened 2 times` for a run that had one sandbox and asks for two at most. The lane reads the line when the gateway has refused a third create, and failed whenever the read fell inside one: 1 time of 6 at a load average of 6.8. With the answer to the third create held 1.5 s by hand the lane failed 3 times of 3 on `7321491`, with that line. A sandbox that is `creating` now counts as open once it has a handle, which is when its provider has answered, and the lane passed 3 of 3 with the answer held. The lane was right and is unchanged.

**A download was broken after a time.** `test/Remote.test.ts` breaks a download twice and asks that it is resumed from the bytes it has. Its server reset the connection 50 ms after it had sent 100,000 bytes, and a download resumes from what its file holds: where the file was still empty after 50 ms the requests were `whole`, `whole`, `bytes=100000-` and not `whole`, `bytes=100000-`, `bytes=200000-`. The server now resets the connection when the file of the download holds the bytes it sent. With the write of each chunk held 100 ms by hand the test failed 3 times of 3 as it was and passes 3 of 3 as it is.

**Fixtures gave an address six seconds.** The three fixtures of closed networks probe five addresses in each phase, each once under `timeout 6`, and the verifier of `closed-agent` once had no answer from `https://example.com/` in that time on krun slots: the row failed for a network that was open. `check.sh` now takes the names of the addresses its caller must reach. The verifier names them. The agent's side reads them from a file `reaches` of the environment, because a scripted agent runs one command for all three fixtures. Such an address is asked again until it answers, and only the timeout of the phase ends that. An address that must not answer keeps its one try of six seconds. A nanocode session returns from a tool call after ten seconds, so on the agent's side of such a session an answer has until then, not longer.

**Leases of three seconds.** The lanes with tasks through the scripted gateway, and the lanes of a sandbox kept warm, leased their sandbox for 3 s and renewed it 3 s before its end, so that a run of seconds renews. A run ends a sandbox by its own clock when its paid time is over, and so does the pool, so no order of events at the gateway keeps a sandbox whose Worker a loaded machine held up for 3 s. The lane then ends with 3 sandboxes where it asks 2, or with a runner that stopped answering: once on ns slots in the pass named above, and on krun slots pinned to two cores 1 time of 12, on `7321491` and on `40e3fea` alike. This one is patience from a measurement, as "free disk floor" has it: each of these lanes adds three times the seconds its Worker took to answer after it was started to the 3 s, for the lease and for the notice. The Worker took 7.2 to 13.3 s here, which gave leases of 25 to 43 s. The start of the runner still waits a lease and a second at the gateway, and a sandbox is kept idle for two leases and 2 s, which is what the 8 s were to 3. With the tick of the run held 7 s once by hand the lane failed 2 times of 2 on `7321491` and passes 2 of 2.

**The end of a kept sandbox.** The pool pays a kept sandbox in whole seconds to the end of its idle time and terminates it when that time ends, so its paid time is over less than a second after the terminate is due. The lane of a kept sandbox asks that the gateway saw the sandbox `terminated` and not `lapsed`: on a loaded machine that was the order of two events less than a second apart, and it says nothing of the pool, which asks for the end either way. Once the pool has paid the kept sandbox to the end of its idle time, the scripted gateway of the lane ends no sandbox for its lease any more, so the end it records is the one the pool asked for. With the pool's terminate held 1.2 s by hand the lane failed 2 times of 2 on `7321491` with `lapsed`, and passes 2 of 2.

**Payments in order.** A run writes a payment down before it sends the request and writes a refusal back when the answer comes, and every lane with a scripted gateway compared the payments of its run with the charges of the gateway in order. The first renewal, which the gateway refuses once with `503`, is in flight beside the write and the exec that start the runner. On krun slots, in a pass of the whole workflow, the write took longer than a tick, the renewal started under it, and its `503` was written back after the intent of the exec: the lane failed on the order of two lists that held the same payments. With the write of the settings of the runner held 1 s and the `503` held 1.5 s by hand the lane failed 2 times of 2 on `7321491` on that line, and passes 2 of 2. The lanes now compare the lists sorted, as the lanes of a kept sandbox did, and still ask that the first payment is the create and the last the terminate.

**A line that could not fail.** The lane of a codex session with direct tools beside one in Code Mode asked that no request declares `spawn_agent`. A session in Code Mode declares `exec` and `wait` alone and is told the tools of its cells in the description of `exec`, one heading each. Read from the request bodies of the lane: 13 headings in 23,162 bytes on `build-f3aa94f`, `spawn_agent` among them, and 5 in 8,456 bytes on the pinned `build-b8158fd`. The scripted model now reads those headings, and the lane asks that the session in Code Mode is told of `exec_command` there, so that the reading is of something, and that neither session has `spawn_agent` as a tool of its own or of its cells. On `build-f3aa94f` the line as it was passes over the requests of the session in Code Mode alone, and the new one fails.

**What each still catches**, with the behaviour it guards broken by hand:

| the resumed download | the resume offset is always 0 | failed: `whole`, `whole`, `whole` |
| tasks through a scripted gateway | the run renews no lease | failed after 607 s: 6 sandboxes where it asks 1, every row an error |
| a sandbox kept warm | the pool terminates no sandbox | failed in 91 s: `undefined` where it asks `terminated`; on ns slots in 170 s |
| a session in Code Mode | the build whose Code Mode names `spawn_agent` | failed: `a codex session is given no tool that starts a subagent` |
| closed networks, installed agents, on krun slots | the slot script never opens the gate of the network | failed after 154 s |
| tasks through a scripted gateway, on krun slots | the run renews no lease | failed after 686 s: 6 sandboxes where it asks 1. The time is the 600 s a row waits for a sandbox |

The lanes took 7.2 to 13.3 s to start their Worker pinned, and the lane of tasks through the gateway 21 s before these changes and 35 s after on the machine unpinned, the kept sandbox 32 s and 71 s: the price of the longer leases.

**On a machine with KVM** (24 cores and 48 threads, kernel 7.0.0-43), beside the other jobs of that machine. Every `run` step of the workflow from fresh clones, twice, on the lanes as they are and then on every change of this entry: 103 of 103 at once both times, the lanes on directory slots in 12.7 of their 20 minutes, on krun slots in 7.8 and 7.9 of 45 and on ns slots in 4.5 and 4.6 of 30. In a unit held to two cores beside two busy loops: tasks through a scripted gateway on krun slots 25 times of 25, where it had failed 1 of 12, in 26 to 32 s after the run that built the launcher, with a Worker that answered after 2.9 to 3.8 s and leases of 12 to 15 s; the same lane on ns slots 10 of 10 in 26 to 29 s; a sandbox kept warm on ns slots 10 of 10 in 60 to 67 s; closed networks on krun slots 10 of 10 and with installed agents 10 of 10, 21 to 23 s each after the first. There too, as a user without a systemd session, `scripts/install-linux.sh` ended with its one line and exit 2, and doctor missed a base URL at a port where nothing listened (`fetch failed: connect ECONNREFUSED`, exit 1) and, once the scripted model was up, printed that it answers and ended `ready for krun slots`.

**A first start from the README on a bare machine.** An operator who had not seen the repository followed "A bare machine", "Quick start" and "Run it locally" as a new user of a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 with KVM, at `7321491`. `nanoeval doctor` named what the machine lacked, each command it printed ran as printed, and the machine part took 41 s; the quick start gave its 4 of 9 on krun slots in 88 s, 72 s of them the build of the launcher, and in 8 s on directory slots; as root, `doctor --backend ns` found nothing missing. Four things were wrong:

- The README said that doctor ends with `ready for krun slots`. With everything installed it ended `1 missing for krun slots` and exit 1, for the model credential that the shell did not hold, until the two variables of the scripted model were exported. The step and the help of the command now say so. A credential stays a miss: a Worker started from such a shell runs `--oracle` only.
- With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` naming a port where nothing listened, every row of a run ended as `errored agent: Messages transport: {"detail":"Network connection lost."}`, and doctor said that the Worker pays through a base URL and that the machine was ready. Doctor now asks each base URL that its shell names for a model, and one where nothing answers is missing, with the address, what was said and what to start. The Worker does not say which base URL it has, so a doctor in another shell than the Worker's still does not see it.

- A bare machine has no `git`, and the steps are read from the clone: the section says so before its first step.

**Rejected.**

- For the status line: a word of its own for the sandbox that is asked for, as in "1 open, 1 asked for". The line is there for a refusal, and "another could not be opened" already is that sandbox.
- For the leases: a run that measures an attached runner first, as the lanes of the entry before this one do. It adds a run to eight lanes on three kinds of slot, and what a lease has to outlast is a Worker that is held up, which the start of the Worker measures at no cost. A longer notice with the lease left at 3 s: a renewal is priced from now to the new end, so each would pay the notice again. Holding the gateway's lapse in these lanes too: the run ends the sandbox by its own clock.
- For the kept sandbox: asking that the sandbox ended either way. The lane would no longer tell a pool that terminates from one that lets a lease run out.
- For the payments: the charges in order and the refusals apart. Two requests in flight can also reach the gateway in the other order.
- For the download and the fixtures: a longer time. 50 ms and six seconds were each enough on a quiet machine and each too short once.

## 2026-11-14: a third reading of the changes above, and what the first rows on a real model asked of status and of the import

The changes of the entry above were read once more before they landed, beside the notes of the first rows that a real model ran on these revisions (eight small tasks of Terminal-Bench 2.1 on ns slots, on a machine with root and without KVM). Three things changed, and one more waits for a decision.

**A machine without KVM imports no disk.** The README said that such a machine "converts a task that names an image, as the datasets do, and not a task with a Dockerfile". It does not. The launcher writes the disk of an image in a builder microVM, as it builds a Dockerfile in one (`krun/host/src/image/build.rs`: both go through `Machine::start`), so the import pulled the image and then failed with `the converter failed at build: ... this build of nanoeval-krun starts no microVM`, and doctor's note for a machine without KVM named Dockerfile tasks alone. The converter now refuses both kinds on a machine that starts no microVM, before the launcher is built and before a layer is pulled, in the line a Dockerfile had, and the README and the note say what such a machine does: it runs disks that were imported where KVM is, or imports with `--backend dir`. Rejected: converting an image without a microVM, in namespaces as root. It is what the operator of those rows did by hand to get on, and it is a second path that writes the same disk, with its own ways to differ.

**A claim that expired says why.** In those rows the local Worker died of a full disk, see below, while a runner worked a row. The Worker came back with its state, the runner was answered that it was lost, and the row passed on its second claim. The status showed `claims=2` on the row and a model spend of $0.0290 over an agent line of $0.0260, and the first claim said `"ending": "expired"` and nothing else. Three things end a claim as expired, and each now writes its reason to the claim, where `nanoeval attempt` shows it: no word of the row from its runner for a lease (`the lease of the attempt ran out: runner 1 sent no word of it for the 60 s that a lease lasts`), which is also all that a Worker which did not run for that long can know; the end of the sandbox of the runner; the end of that sandbox's lease. The status of a run carries its last lost claim, and the command prints one line: how many claims were lost, that their model calls are in the spend of the run and in the cost of no agent, and the last one with its reason. That sentence is the difference of the two figures above: the spend counts the sessions of lost claims, and an agent's line sums results, which a lost claim does not have. The line does not give the amount: with a priced route the requests of a lost claim are rows of the same table as the others, and a figure there needs the same care as the spend itself. Rejected: one line for each lost claim, which is a screen of them when a sandbox with eight rows ends.

**The link of libkrunfw.** The change above left an installed library that is the release's as it is and still wrote its link `libkrunfw.so.5` again with `ln -sf`, which removes the link and makes it anew, so a microVM that loads the library between the two still does not find it. `scripts/ci-machine.sh` writes the link only when it does not name the library.

**Not changed: a slot that fills the disk of its machine.** One of those rows grew the copy-on-write disk of its slot to 9.9 GB of the 10 GB its task may use (`storage_mb`) within about 100 s; the same task used 2.2 to 2.6 GB in five other rows. The machine had 16 GB free, shared with other work, and filled: the local Worker logged `SQLITE_IOERR_SHMSIZE` and was gone 22 s later. `--free-disk-mb` is a floor that a runner reads when it claims, with one row starting at a time. It does not count what the rows in flight may still write, and a run that does not name it has no floor. What would hold: a runner admits a row only while the free disk, less what each of its rows in flight may still write (its `storage_mb` less the size of its disk now), less the `storage_mb` of the new row, stays at or above the floor. On that machine the first row of 10 GB is admitted at 16 GB free and a second waits until the first has ended, where two ran. The cost is rows that wait on a machine that would have been large enough: at 2.6 GB used of 10 GB reserved, four slots need 40 GB free to run four such rows at once where 10.4 GB are written. It changes how many rows a machine runs at once, and for a leased sandbox whether a run of rows with large `storage_mb` starts at all, so it waits for a decision and a lane of its own, and is not in this change. Until then: keep slots times the largest `storage_mb` free, or name `--free-disk-mb` with that margin.

**Read again and left as they are.** The lane of a kept sandbox no longer tells a pool that terminates at the end of the idle time from one that terminates late: once the pool has paid to that end, the scripted gateway lets no lease lapse. It still fails when the pool terminates nothing, pays less than the idle time or leaves the end to the gateway before that point. The lanes with a scripted gateway compare payments and charges as sets with their counts, and still ask for the create first and the terminate last. The download test waits for the bytes in the file with no bound of its own: a download that never writes them stops the test command, where it failed a line before. `test/Sandbox.test.ts` looks for the process of its slot by its command line on the whole machine, so two `npm test` at once on one machine fail each other in "taking a slot down ends the work it still runs": seen here once, and it passes alone.

**Checked.** On the machine of the entry above, 5 cores and no KVM, every command with a lane slot of its own. `npm run lint` and `npm run check:types` pass. `npm test`: 380 tests, 375 passed, 5 skipped for KVM or root, 0 failed, in 79 s. Unit tests: the refusal of an image beside the three of a Dockerfile (`test/Converter.test.ts`), doctor's note (`test/Doctor.test.ts`), the line of the status with and without a reason and for a Worker that sends none (`test/Summary.test.ts`). The lane of a runner lost during a run, on directory slots with a lease of 3 s, now reads the reason of the expired claim and the line of the status: 3 times of 3, in 21 to 24 s. For the link, the two lines of the script run twice against a directory made for it wrote the link once.

**Not verified.** No lane on krun or ns slots ran with these changes: the lane of a lost runner on krun slots reads the same two things. `scripts/ci-machine.sh` was not run. The reasons of a sandbox that ended and of a lease that ended are written by the same call as the first and were not read in a lane. The refusal of an image was not run from the command on a machine with root and no KVM.

## 2026-11-14: a slot reads the metadata of a cached disk in one open

**What was wrong.** A runner describes a cached disk for every attempt and for every row it fetches ahead: `sandbox/Host.ts` writes the three files beside the disk (`.env`, `.user`, `.workdir`) to a temporary name and renames each over the file, since f67b6f3. `sandbox/slot.sh` copied two of them into the slot with `cp`. GNU cp looks at a file, then opens it, and refuses when the two are not the same file: `cp: skipping file '….env', as it was replaced while being copied`. A slot that came up on a disk already in the cache while its runner described that disk again for a row ahead failed its environment, and its row ended as an `environment` error 76 ms after its claim. It was seen once, in the lane of a sandbox kept warm for a second run on ns slots, whose second run starts at once on cached disks: that run ended with 2 passed and 1 errored where 3 passed are asked. Any krun or ns row whose disk is cached while another row of that disk is prepared could meet it, in a real run as in a lane.

**What changed.** The slot reads each of the two files through one open (`cat FILE >COPY`), as it already read the working directory. A reader that holds the file open reads the old content or the new, whole, whichever the rename left under the name.

**Checked.** On a 24-core machine with KVM (kernel 7.0, GNU coreutils 9.4), one writer that replaces a file by rename against one reader for ten seconds: `cp` failed 32 of 9,914 copies, `cat` none of 12,441. With the change on an earlier base (main at 40e3fea and the changes above), on that machine: every run step of `ci.yml` from fresh clones, 103 of 103, and the lane of the kept sandbox on ns slots alone, 8 of 8.

**Not verified.** That the change removes the failure in the lane itself: the lane failed once in 15 runs without it, which is no rate to measure against. No test holds the race, since one would be a test of a time.

**Landed on a later main.** The changes from the entry "two local Workers that start at the same moment" to this one were written on main at `40e3fea` and landed on main at `8adf95d`, ten commits later, and the counts in the entries above are of the bases they name. Main's commits are as they were. Two lanes follow its pin of nanocode-ts `build-a7fdac2`, which leaves the cell of a codex session none of the Claude Code hand tools, and its check of the tools that the cells of a codex session list: the cells of the lane that kills the Worker while one of two cells still runs call `exec_command` where they called `Bash` and print their tools, and the lane of a session with direct tools records the description of `exec` only for the requests that declare it. On that form, from fresh clones on a machine with 5 cores and no KVM: `npm run lint`, `npm run check:types` and `npm run dry-run` pass; `npm test`: 396 tests, 391 passed, 5 skipped for KVM or root, 0 failed; the 51 lanes of the job `e2e-dir` and the two of `e2e-revision` passed at the first try, two at a time; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` in `krun/` pass. The krun and ns lanes skip themselves on that machine. On a machine with KVM (24 cores, kernel 7.0), every run step of `ci.yml` from fresh clones, beside the same steps of main and an import of the 89 tasks of Terminal-Bench 2.1: 103 of 104 passed at the first try, the 29 krun lanes and the 12 ns lanes among them, and no lane skipped itself. The one that did not is the lane of a provider that refuses sandboxes for a cap, on directory slots. The scripted gateway refuses the first renewal of a run with 503, and while the machine was at its busiest, with calls to the gateway that took up to a second, the next renewal of the first sandbox was answered after its lease of 3 s had ended. The run opened another sandbox, and the lane, which ends the first sandbox the gateway opened, ended the one that was gone and not the one that served: the row it waits for kept its runner, and the lane failed after 315 s with `the capped happened during the run`. ## 2026-11-14: libkrun never blocks its vsock thread on a slow host socket, libkrun `2dad364`

**The cause.** The entry "the host relay of a slot always reads what its guest sends" left the root of that stall in libkrun: its proxies for stream vsock connections (`src/devices/src/virtio/vsock/unix.rs` for a guest-initiated or guest-listening port, `tsi_stream.rs` for TSI) wrote what the guest sent with a blocking `send` on the thread that processes the guest's transmit queue. That queue also carries the guest's credit updates and every other connection's packets, so one host reader that stopped reading froze every vsock connection of the microVM, `exec` included. The relay's drain of 8adf95d only kept nanoeval's own relay from being that slow reader.

**The rule.** libkrun `2dad364` (nanocodexyz/libkrun, branch `vsock-credit-request-irq`, on top of the `8ce363e` this repository pinned) sends with `MSG_DONTWAIT` and keeps what the host socket does not take in a buffer per connection (`stream_tx.rs`). The buffer is bounded by the `buf_alloc` libkrun advertises to the guest (8 MiB): `fwd_cnt`, in data headers, credit updates and credit requests alike, advances only as bytes leave the buffer, so a guest that keeps to its credit cannot grow it past that, and one that does not is reset. While bytes are kept the proxy polls the socket for `EPOLLOUT`, flushes, and sends a credit update each time half of the smaller `buf_alloc` has left. A write shutdown from the guest waits until the buffer is empty, and a connection the guest resets keeps flushing before it is reaped. Both vsock threads now set a proxy's epoll interest while they hold its lock, so neither applies an older interest after the other's newer one. The relay's drain of 8adf95d stays: it keeps the relay from holding bytes back from its upstream.

**Checked** on dev-georgios (load average 150 to 300 from the live runners, one run each unless counted): `a_host_reader_that_stalls_leaves_every_other_connection_answering` in `host/tests/image.rs` boots a microVM from an image with a static busybox, has a guest `exec` write 64 MiB through a forward to the test's own `relay.sock`, which accepts and then reads nothing for 30 s while `exec -- /bin/guest oom-kills` must answer within 10 s every second, then reads all 64 MiB and the end of the stream and asks `exec` once more. With libkrun `8ce363e` the first `exec` of the stall did not answer in 10 s; with `2dad364` every one answered and the 64 MiB arrived whole. The data crossed both proxies: the guest's TCP connection to the forward goes through TSI and the forward's vsock connection through `unix.rs`, and libkrun's debug log of one run showed each forwarding all 67,108,864 bytes. The writing `exec` does not end after its stream is read, with `8ce363e` and no stall as well, so the test stops it instead of waiting for it. libkrun's own unit tests of the buffer (`cargo test -p krun-devices stream_tx`: a stalled reader never blocks the writer, credit follows bytes that left the buffer, a write shutdown waits for kept bytes) and `cargo clippy --locked --features net,blk -- -D warnings` pass. In `krun/`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` with the KVM tests pass.

**Release.** The launcher links libkrun statically: a machine takes this when its `NANOEVAL_KRUN` binaries are rebuilt from this commit, and a slot when its microVM next starts. dev-georgios runs `~/nc-live/krunfull`, which predates both `8ce363e` and this change.
## 2026-11-12: nanocode's own command line as an installed agent, and imports without KVM

Machines: a 5-core, 14 GiB Linux Hand with no KVM and no root, whose only egress is an HTTP proxy that re-signs TLS, and E2B `desktop` sandboxes (8 vCPUs, 7,955 MB) leased from the Tempo gateway with one Tempo Key. Node 24.22.2 in the sandbox, nanocode CLI 0.7.0 (the pinned `nanocode-cli` release, and a build of 0.7.0 with a patch that gives `--harness claude` a Messages endpoint and lets a custom model follow `--harness`). Model `boundless/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` through the gateway.

### What was built

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `nanocode-codex` and `nanocode-claude` installed agents | `ID=nanocode-codex:MODEL[:THINKING]` runs `nanocode exec --ephemeral --no-subagents --no-tempo-tools --harness codex -m MODEL -t THINKING -- INSTRUCTION` inside the slot, `nanocode-claude` the same with `--harness claude`. The binary is the slot's runtime nanocode, the one its hand runs (`/opt/nanoeval/nanocode` with the runtime's loader and libraries, or `NANOEVAL_NANOCODE`), so nothing more is fetched. Codex reads `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `NANOCODE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, Claude `NANOCODE_ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES_URL`, `NANOCODE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `NANOCODE_MODELS_URL`: each is the attempt's endpoint and token, never a credential |
| `GET models` on the run's model endpoint for nanocode agents | nanocode lists the models of a custom endpoint before it starts. The run answers with the agent's own model and forwards nothing |
| Image conversion without KVM | The launcher built without libkrun now answers `vm` for an image build with a mount namespace instead of a builder microVM: the build disk loop-mounted at `/mnt/root` and the guest agent serving `vm.sock` in `ns-serve` mode, as root. Layers are applied by the same guest code. A Dockerfile build, which needs a builder that runs steps, is refused |
| `deep-swe-1.1` | Pinned in the catalog: `datacurve/deep-swe-1-1` at `sha256:5affcd53…`, 113 tasks whose digests hash to `sha256:395be8f1…`. `import deep-swe-1.1 --out DIR` writes checked task directories. It is not importable as an eval, see below |

### What was decided

- **Two kinds, not one with a harness option.** The agent syntax has one slot for the harness, and each kind has one provider route of the run (Responses or Messages), which is what the credential swap and the meter already key on.
- **`--no-subagents`.** A leaderboard fixes one model and effort per eval. A subagent may pick another model, so the agent gets none.
- **The output is the final message.** `nanocode exec` streams the reply to stdout and reasoning and tool calls to stderr, with no JSON mode. The trajectory holds the instruction and the reply. stderr is kept as `agent/stderr.txt`, and tokens and cost come from the run's meter.
- **The control plane in a sandbox.** The Hand reaches the internet only through its proxy and may not expose a port (Tailscale Funnel is not allowed for the node, and a quick tunnel needs direct egress). The Worker runs under local workerd in a gateway sandbox created with `ports: [8787]`, so the CLI on the Hand and runners in other sandboxes reach it at its public URL. The Worker holds `TEMPO_KEY`, which no slot can read: slots are chrooted, in their own PID namespace and dropped from the sandbox's addresses.

### Measurements

Import of three Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks (`fix-git`, `log-summary-date-ranges`, `openssl-selfsigned-cert`) in the control-plane sandbox, no KVM: 12.7 s, conversions of 2.4 to 4.1 s. Oracle on ns slots in the same sandbox: 3 of 3 passed in about 25 s.

| Run | Rows | Slots at once | Result | Attempt median (min to max) | Run wall | Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nanocode-codex`, GLM-5.3-Flash high, stock release | 3 tasks x 3 | 3 | 8 passed, 1 failed | 44.6 s (27.0 to 62.2) | 157.5 s | $0.0432 |
| `nanocode-claude`, GLM-5.3-Flash high, patched build | 3 tasks x 2 | 6 (runner `--memory-mb 15000`) | 6 passed | 53.0 s (50.5 to 62.2) | 64.4 s | $0.0210 |
| Both kinds, 3 tasks x 4 each | 24 | 7 | 19 errored, 5 cancelled | | 150.6 s | $0.0080 |
| Oracle, `--provider gateway`: the Worker leased a `desktop` sandbox with its key and started the runner from the runtime archive | 3 | 3 | 3 passed | | 45 s | sandbox $0.0445 |

An attempt's environment came up in 0.3 s, and its verifier took 6 to 8 s with three slots and 9 to 16 s with six. With seven slots the sandbox's load average stayed under 0.7 and its memory under 1.8 GB: the slots of a `desktop` sandbox are bound by the memory the tasks declare, three of 2 GiB at the runner's rule. The run of 24 errored on the model, not the machine: the gateway answered `502 upstream_failed`, "boundless HTTP 402 ... voucher cumulativeAmount must be strictly greater than highest accepted voucher", for both routes, while another lane sent about five requests at once on the same key. The errors stayed errors. Minutes later the same answer came to single serial requests.

### What DeepSWE v1.1 needs

Its tasks declare task schema 1.3, `[verifier] environment_mode = "separate"` with a `tests/Dockerfile` of the task image plus the tests, a `[[verifier.collect]]` hook that writes `/logs/artifacts/model.patch` in the agent's environment, `artifacts` carried into the verifier's, `network_mode = "no-network"` for the agent and the verifier, 2 CPUs, 8 GiB and 20 GB for each environment, and `reward.json`. nanoeval refuses the schema and the separate verifier, does not run collect hooks or read `reward.json`, closes a network only on krun slots, and a `desktop` sandbox admits no row of 8 GiB.

### Not verified

- An installed agent whose task closes its network, on any slot.
- A model run through `--provider gateway`: the gateway's Boundless route failed before one was attempted.

## 2026-11-14: a verifier that leaves reward.txt without a reward is an environment error, retried once

A verifier whose reward.txt exists but holds no number, such as a zero-byte file from a write that a full disk or a killed process cut, was a `verifier` error and was never retried, the same as a verifier that wrote no reward at all. It was not a score, so no task failure was counted, but the attempt was lost to an infrastructure cause. `Verdict.verifier` now makes such an attempt an `environment` error whose message starts with `Verdict.emptyRewardPrefix` (unless the log already names a cause, such as a full disk), and `Retry.infrastructure` returns a cause for it, so the run ends the claim `retried` and starts the row once more from nothing, as it does for a slot out of disk. A verifier that writes no reward.txt stays a `verifier` error and is not retried. A verifier timeout keeps its kind. nanoeval reads no reward.json, so only reward.txt applies.

Check: `output/empty-reward/check.ts` (ignored) writes each case into a slot's verifier directory, lists it with `slot.sh files`, parses the reward as the runner does, and passes it to `Verdict.verifier` and `Retry.infrastructure`. Hosted Hand, Linux x86_64, Node 24, one run each:

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zero-byte reward.txt | `verifier`, not retried | `environment`, retried |
| reward.txt with only a newline | `verifier`, not retried | `environment`, retried |
| no reward.txt | `verifier`, not retried | `verifier`, not retried |
| reward 0 | scored 0 | scored 0 |

Retried: 0 of 4 before, 2 of 4 after. `node --test test/Retry.test.ts` with the new test: 4 pass, 1 fail on `src/Verdict.ts` and `src/Retry.ts` of the parent commit, 5 pass with the change.
